correctness.rationale: Translate to centers 0,d and scale each nonzero coordinate to 1 by a node-metric isometry. At d=0, pairwise star overlaps share one nonloop coordinate, and no three contain a nonzero common word. For τ>2 no two stars can support d. At τ=1, the two possible singleton covers of a lone nonloop edge give the two-star union. For a unique singleton cover v, only the two-spoke loopless support admits a two-star decomposition avoiding v; each orientation of its two other endpoints adds exactly q−1 points outside V_v and these additions are disjoint. At τ=2, each oriented cover gives a q-point affine line. Coincidence of one index gives a unique intersection via the common off-star edge, while coincidence of neither requires two nonzero disjoint edges, forcing exactly the matching support. Outside that case three pairwise intersecting lines would need a common first or second index i and three distinct partner stars; their common nonzero off-star support is impossible. The matching has two disjoint groups of four lines, each with one shared point. This proves 2qc−2h+2m, including the correction to ordinary pairwise subtraction. Independently computed the ordered differences of one-ball words, tabulated multiplicities, and matched every unit-valued support for (n,q)=(4,2),(4,3),(4,4),(5,2), 35,840 cases in total, via branches/reproduction/overlap.py. The uniform result rests on the affine proof, not the finite sample. The frozen verifier was inspected, not executed.
